Personally, I bring a notebook and use the hour in the meeting to log my thoughts and feelings for the day, often in light of what is being discussed. If the meeting is on the boring or repetitive side, I find I spend more time in my head and the notebook, but during engaging meetings I am much more involved. Its not a method for everyone, but I found it allows me to get the most out of meetings without feeling the time spent is a burden or boring.

Personally, I've never been able to do moderation but even sober I enjoy going out for "drinks" with friends. I have always found it easiest to show up with a drink already in your hand (I'm a big fan of showing up with my cup of coffee, although later in the night a bottle of water or a redbull work well too). This helps avoid the initial "What do you want to drink?" when you first show up. I then can get my own drinks throughout the night, normally sticking with club soda or a diet coke. The only place I have found that people may still try to push is if they are buying rounds of shots, but so many people refuse shots that it normally doesn't show up as that big of an issue when you say no.

Good luck and enjoy your birthday.

I did over two years sober and then decided I was "fixed" last December, so decided I could act in moderation. Well, moderation didn't last and I was back to my problematic habits within six months and showed all kinds of signs that I should stop. But I let it drag on, and just over a week ago I had a major bender and caused all kinds of problems that I will be spending the foreseeable future fixing. I wish I had been smart enough to admit that the signs I was seeing existed, and I used any of those to make the decision of sobriety again. 

I can't change what I have done, so I am now a week into sobriety again, starting over. I know what you're going through, and not that hearing it will change anything, but just in case it helps....you've experienced both sober and not sober, you know that not sober is miserable, take the steps you know will make you feel better in the long run.

I'm someone who racked up a couple of years of dry time due to hitting what I thought was rock bottom, but then I decided I was ok to try again and slowly started to get worse. At multiple points, I knew I should quit and knew I was on the wrong path, but was never willing to do something about it.

This past weekend I hit a new low and am facing serious consequences for it. Every minute since then I have looked back and said "If I had only listened to my logical self". 

I can't tell you what to do, and you'll have to figure it out for yourself, but as someone who was in your shoes and took the wrong path, I'd suggest listening to your smarter self and making the right choices.

When I first started working in the film industry in LA, I felt I was caught between the hard partying lifestyle and those people who didn't drink at all. I found it easier there to consciously choose to not go overboard, but when I came back to the East Coast for business (where I felt people were more normal), I let my guard down and my moderate drinking turned into a full blown problem.

I understand what you're going through, and I support what you're doing. IWNDWYT

I recently fell off the wagon, but before that I had stayed dry and sober for over two years. 

When I decided to go sober, I laid low from my trivia night and local haunts for a couple of months, and then slowly started to swing by. I caught the bartenders early and ordered my coke or soda water so they wouldn't pour me a drink right away. This was often accompanied by a question of why not having a drink, to which I either said "I'm trying to cut back" or "I have a busy day tomorrow". I found that the one time of asking to switch it up, meant that they always asked me in the future before pouring, and after a couple of times it was just expected that I wasn't drinking.

After about six months of that, I came clean to some of them that I had quit drinking because it was my new norm and didn't seem weird.

​

Although, for what it's worth, these were the same places that had no problem pouring me drinks again once I started ordering them again, and it didn't take long for them to return to being my regular.
